paper.title: New Block Cipher: ARIA (algorithm as specified in RFC 5794)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: ARIA (12/14/16 rounds, substitution layers SL1/SL2 over SB1-SB4, 16-byte diffusion layer A, 3-round Feistel key schedule with the C1-C3 constants, odd/even round functions FO/FE) written from RFC 5794 reproduces the Appendix A example data: for the 128-bit key W0-W3 (4), encryption round keys e1-e13 (13) and intermediate round values P1-P11 (11); and the ciphertexts for the 128-, 192- and 256-bit example keys (3)
Decryption with the derived decryption round keys returns the plaintext for the three example keys (3)

The RFC's statements that SB3/SB4 are the inverses of SB1/SB2 (512 entries), the two worked S-box examples, and that A is an involution (on 16 test inputs, a sample not a proof) hold for the table data

expected_values_source.what: RFC 5794 section 2.2/2.4 (constants, S-boxes) and Appendix A (example data)
expected_values_source.note: the tables and vectors were copied as data by script from the fetched text; the program was written from the RFC's description. The ICISC 2003 paper itself was not fetched; Appendix A gives intermediate values for the 128-bit key only, the 192- and 256-bit keys are checked at the ciphertext only

negative_control: built with -DARIA_R19=18 (the first round-key rotation of 19 bits changed to 18), 18 published values mismatch including all three ciphertexts and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security and performance claims (resistance to differential/linear attacks, cycle counts)
that C1-C3 are the first 384 fractional bits of 1/pi (taken from the RFC as data, not recomputed)
other keys and plaintexts than the three RFC examples, modes of operation and the RFC's OIDs
speed (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 34 intermediate values, ciphertexts and decryptions RFC 5794 publishes for its examples. It does not show the security claims hold.
